item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E015","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E017","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Scholz proposed a cross-government Deutschlandpakt with Länder, municipalities, opposition, businesses, and unions to accelerate energy, housing, infrastructure, digital administration, and permitting; he cited 85 percent federal online-service implementation, versus one quarter at Länder and municipal level.","notes":["The excerpt supports the proposal, policy areas, and implementation percentages, but not the September 2023 date."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E018","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Scholz said the government planned €24 billion of additional rail investment over four years, €18 billion for subsidized housing, €58 billion in investment in the coming year through the climate-transformation fund, and €54 billion in federal investment in rail, bridges, internet, and charging infrastructure.","notes":["The excerpt states €58 billion for the coming year, but does not itself identify that year as 2024."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E019","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Scholz cited Intel's €30 billion investment in Magdeburg as the largest foreign single investment in Europe's history and mentioned additional semiconductor investments in Germany.","notes":["The excerpt does not contain the claim that more than €80 billion had been invested by international companies across future industries."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E020","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E021","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The Bundestag approved the Pflegeunterstützungs- und -entlastungsgesetz on 26 May 2023, providing improvements for people needing care and relatives, stabilizing long-term-care insurance finances, improving working conditions for professional caregivers, and strengthening digitalization in long-term care.","notes":["The excerpt says the Bundestag approved the bill in second/third reading; it does not expressly state final enactment as a law."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E022","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E023","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E024","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E025","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On 16 November 2023, the Bundestag approved the coalition's amendment to the Federal Expellees Act by a broad majority; it enabled a return toward the earlier administrative practice and enabled authorities to provide information from relevant records and administrative files to help preserve recipients' ability to prove their status, while rejecting the AfD alternative.","notes":["The excerpt supports enabling authorities to provide information and preventing later inability to prove status; it does not expressly say that the amendment authorized preservation of records."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E026","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E027","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0033-E028","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
